title: Keep the audit log's type names when a constant gets a body

blocks.text: The order service writes an audit line for every field of an order that changes: `discount: Discount NONE -> VOUCHER`, or `total: type changed from Amount to Channel` when the old and the new value are not of the same type. Since `LOYALTY` and `VOUCHER` got discount rules of their own, the audit log has gone wrong for them: some lines name no type at all, and a customer moving from no discount to a voucher is logged as a change of type.

items: `typeName(value)`: the name the log shows for the value's type;
`sameType(a, b)`: whether a change from `a` to `b` is an edit of one type.

blocks.text: When you're done, every constant of `Discount` is logged as a `Discount`, whichever constant it is, and a constant of one enum is never the same type as a constant of another. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a constant without a body and a record are shown with the simple name of their type
two constants of one plain enum, or two records of one class, are the same type; values of different types are not
an edit between two plain constants is written with the enum's name, and a change of type is written as such
a constant that overrides a method in a body of its own is shown with its enum's name, not a blank
a constant with a body is the same type as the other constants of its enum, with or without bodies, and not the same type as another enum's constant

origin.section: A Constant With a Body Is an Anonymous Subclass, So getClass() Isn't the Enum

concepts: A constant with a body is an instance of an anonymous subclass, so getClass() is not the enum for it; getDeclaringClass() is, and switch, EnumSet and EnumMap are unaffected.
